landing.method.title: How we build a score
landing.method.sources.title: Sources
landing.method.sources.text: NSE and BSE filings, company IR decks and guidance tables, earnings-call transcripts.
landing.method.guidance.title: What counts as guidance
landing.method.guidance.text: A number or range for a named metric and period, taken from a filing, results release or call transcript. Commentary without a number is left out. If guidance is raised or cut during the year, we score against the original number and show every revision next to it.
landing.method.review.title: Verification
landing.method.review.text: Each guidance quote and each reported actual is kept with its document link and date. The row counts only when a fetch of both documents contains those quotes. The company page shows the date of that check.
landing.method.score.title: Scoring
landing.method.score.text: GCI scores promise-keeping, not forecast accuracy. Each closed result earns 0–100 points for where it landed against its own guided range: 100 inside the range, fewer the further outside. A revenue-growth miss and a margin miss share that scale when each is the same distance outside its own range. A wide range reaches 100 more easily than a tight one. Misses lose points faster than beats. A company's score is the evidence-weighted average of its metrics. Each metric counts in proportion to how many closed years it has (up to five), and once a deeper metric exists, a metric with a single closed year is shown as context and not scored. Recent years weigh more. Scores are not adjusted by sector. Open periods don't count until results are filed. A score changes when the filing check confirms the new result, and every change is listed in the changelog.

about.what.title: What it is
about.what.p1: CiteAlpha is a product of Ocotillo Innovation Private Limited. It publishes the Guidance Credibility Index (GCI), a 0–100 score of whether the management of an Indian listed company delivered on its quantified guidance. Think of it as a credit score for promises against actuals. It is not a sentiment dashboard or a price terminal.
about.what.li1: Every citeable score links to the period, metric, guided range, actual, outcome and source (URL, quote and citation ID).
about.what.li2: India first. Sensex companies have hand-labeled evidence; other NSE/BSE listings can be browsed, each with a badge that shows its data quality.
about.what.li3: We do not offer Buy / Hold / Sell views, retail tips, order management or live quotes.
about.why.title: Why it is needed
about.why.lede: Desks already have news, filing search and market terminals. What they lack is a sourced record of whether a management team kept its word.
about.why.drift.title: Guidance drifts
about.why.drift.text: Ranges move mid-year, and guidance that is quietly dropped is soon forgotten. Without a linked record from statement to actual, a pattern of misses stays anecdotal.
about.why.india.title: India-shaped disclosure
about.why.india.text: NSE/BSE filings, IR tables, mixed-language concalls and local reporting formats need a product built for India, not a US product with India added later.
about.why.compliance.title: Compliance
about.why.compliance.text: Factual delivery research stays on the right side of SEBI Research Analyst rules. Analysts own the forecasts; CiteAlpha shows observed delivery and its citations.
about.why.hitl.title: Corrections that accumulate
about.why.hitl.text: Each extract is reviewed and committed, so desk corrections build a lasting labeled record instead of a one-off spreadsheet paste.
about.how.title: How it works
about.how.lede: One pipeline takes a document from ingestion to a searchable, citable record. Citation only works if documents are stored with their structure intact, so it is built in from the first step.
about.pipeline.1.title: Ingest
about.pipeline.1.text: IR pages, transcripts and filings are collected into the document store, starting with a crawl of Sensex companies. Pasting a document by hand is the fallback.
about.pipeline.2.title: Extract & review
about.pipeline.2.text: Quantified guidance is extracted as pending statements. An analyst accepts, edits or rejects each one before it can affect a score.
about.pipeline.3.title: Match & score
about.pipeline.3.text: Each guided range is matched to the reported actual and labeled met, exceeded, missed, dropped or pending. Those outcomes roll up into a 0–100 company GCI.
about.pipeline.4.title: Cite
about.pipeline.4.text: Every citeable data point carries its period, metric, quote, URL and a citation ID tied to an accepted document.
about.how.note: Badges show data quality. Only hand-labeled companies are fit for external citation. Provisional listings are scored for screening only, and we never invent a citeable quote. Analytics overlays (such as GCI against the share price) describe past patterns and are not forecasts. Granger panels show statistical precedence only.
about.layers.title: Capability layers
about.layers.lede: These describe what the product does, not what you buy. Seats and API access are on the Package page. Annotated screenshots are in the tier gallery.
about.layers.foundation.title: Foundation
about.layers.foundation.text: Automatic ingestion of each period's documents (transcript, results, IR), company search that shows what is actually in the document store, and a citation ID for every citeable item. The Corpus tab in the Analyst Workbench tracks Sensex coverage.
about.layers.workflow.title: Workflow
about.layers.workflow.text: Changes over several horizons (QoQ and YoY from point-in-time history), descriptive GCI-against-price overlays, private notes, and report templates by role with a citation appendix.
about.layers.analytics.title: Analytics (gated)

about.layers.oos.text: Buy/Hold/Sell, treating a provisional listing score as citeable IR evidence, or copying a global market-intelligence platform.

method.page.title: How the Guidance Credibility Index is built
method.page.lede: GCI is a 0–100 score of promise-keeping: how reliably reported results landed against the numbers management guided to. It does not measure forecast accuracy, sentiment or share price, or whether the results were good news.
method.page.guidance.title: 1. What counts as guidance
method.page.guidance.i1: A number or range for a named metric and a named period, for example "revenue growth of 13%–15% in constant currency for FY23".
method.page.guidance.i2: It must come from a primary source: an exchange filing (NSE, BSE, or the SEC for dual-listed companies), a company results release or investor deck, or an earnings-call transcript.
method.page.guidance.i3: Commentary without a number ("we expect a strong year") is recorded as unmapped and never scored.
method.page.review.title: 2. Check against the filing
method.page.review.i1: Each guidance quote and each reported actual is stored with its document link and date.
method.page.review.i2: The row counts only when a fetch of both documents contains those quotes. Companies whose rows have not passed that check show "Not yet scored".
method.page.review.i3: A score changes when a newly filed result passes that check. For filings dated on or after 29 Sep 2026, the score is published within 5 business days of the results filing. A news headline does not move a score.
method.page.review.i4: A closed row counts when a fetch of the guidance filing and the results filing both contain the recorded quotes. The company page shows the date of that check. A quote that is not on the filing keeps the row out of the score.
method.page.sla.title: Filing to score
method.page.sla.target: Target: the score is published within {days} business days of the results filing (India Monday–Friday), for filings dated on or after {since}, once both quotes are on the filings.
method.page.sla.live: Observed (live sample): median {median} business days across {n} rows.
method.page.sla.liveEmpty: Observed (live sample): none yet. No filings dated on or after {since} have been scored.
method.page.sla.backfill: Historical batch ({n} rows, checked {reviewedOn}): median {median} business days from the original results filing to that check. Those rows were added after the fact and are not measured against the 5-day target.
method.page.revisions.title: 3. When guidance is raised or cut during the year
method.page.revisions.p1: The score uses the original guidance, the number management gave at the start of the period. That is the promise investors priced in, and GCI asks whether it held.
method.page.revisions.p2: Every later revision is recorded next to the original with its own date and source, along with a second outcome measured against the final revised range. That second outcome is shown for context and is not part of the score. A revision is not treated as withdrawn guidance.
method.page.revisions.example: Example: Infosys guided FY23 revenue growth of 13%–15%, raised it three times to 16.0%–16.5%, and delivered 15.4%. Against the original range that is exceeded; against the final range it is missed. Both are shown on the company page:
method.page.formula.title: 4. Scoring one result
method.page.formula.intro: Each closed result (guidance plus its reported actual) earns 0–100 points:
method.page.formula.inside.label: Inside the guided range:
method.page.formula.inside.text: 100 points. A range narrower than 2% of its midpoint is widened to ±2%. For percentage metrics such as margins and growth, the range is never narrower than ±0.1 percentage point.
method.page.formula.outside.label: Outside the range:
method.page.formula.outside.text1: we measure the distance outside in units of the range's half-width, δ. Points decay as
method.page.formula.outside.text2: , so small misses cost a little and large misses cost a lot.
method.page.formula.beats.label: Beats
method.page.formula.beats.text: (the better side of the range) decay from 100 toward a floor of 60 and never go below it. For most metrics that is above the range; for working-capital days it is below. For capex and R&D spend, missing the range in either direction counts as a miss.
method.page.formula.misses.label: Misses
method.page.formula.misses.text: (the worse side of the range) lose points 1.4 times as fast and can reach 0.
method.page.formula.philosophy: GCI measures promise-keeping discipline, not forecast accuracy. A company that beats by a wide margin is scored on how reliable its promise was, not how much upside it delivered.
method.page.formula.floor.label: Why the floor of 60 for beats?
method.page.formula.floor.text: A wide beat scores below 100 because the result landed outside the original range. Under-promising is a smaller credibility problem than over-promising, so any beat stays at or above 60, and a material miss can reach 0. The floor of 60 is a design choice.
method.page.formula.constants.label: Why these numbers?
method.page.formula.constants.text: A miss one half-width outside the guided range scores about 59, about 41 points below a result inside the range, because misses lose points 1.4 times as fast as the underlying decay. A beat the same distance scores about 88 and stays at or above 60. A single-number guide is treated as a ±2% range around that number, and never less than ±0.1 percentage point for a percentage metric. Withdrawing guidance deducts 15 points, a restatement deducts 15, and conflicting guidance for the same period deducts 10. The most recent year weighs 1.0, the year before 0.86, then 0.74. These constants are design choices, published so a reader can judge them.
method.page.formula.example: Example: Infosys guided FY22 revenue growth of 12%–14% (midpoint 13%, half-width 1 point) and grew 19.7%. That is 5.7 half-widths above the range, so the row scores about 62. A miss the same distance below the range would score 0.
method.page.company.title: 5. From results to a company score
method.page.company.metric.label: Per metric:
method.page.company.metric.text: a weighted average of that metric's results. The most recent year has weight 1.0, the year before 0.86, then 0.74, and so on. Rows labeled with lower source confidence count slightly less.
method.page.company.company.label: Per company:
method.page.company.company.text: the evidence-weighted average of its metric scores. Each metric's weight equals its number of closed reporting periods, capped at five. A metric with only one closed period is shown as context and does not enter the score when another metric has two or more; if every metric has a single period, the score is a plain average and carries the provisional tier.
method.page.company.deductions.label: Deductions:
method.page.company.deductions.text: 15 points if guidance was withdrawn, 15 points for a restatement, and 10 points when two reviewed rows give conflicting guidance for the same guidance thread and period.
method.page.company.open.label: Open periods
method.page.company.open.text: (guidance given, results not yet filed) are shown as pending and not counted.
method.page.company.history: Every score carries a confidence tier: provisional (fewer than three closed periods, or one metric), established (three or more periods, two or more metrics) or deep (five or more periods, two or more metrics). A metric counts toward breadth once it has one closed result confirmed against its filing, whether it enters the composite or is shown as context. A closed result scores only when both the original guidance and the subsequent actual are cited; rows missing the guidance citation are shown as pending guidance cite and do not enter the score. Only established and deep scores are ranked on the Public Snapshot. Most scored companies are provisional today.
method.page.company.record: Next to the score we show the delivery record (how many results came in above, inside or below guidance), so the direction of any miss is visible separately from the score.
method.page.company.comparable.label: Across metrics and sectors
method.page.company.comparable.text: A revenue-growth miss and a margin miss share the 0–100 scale when each is the same distance outside its own guided range, measured in that range's half-width. A wide range reaches 100 more easily than a tight one. Scores are not adjusted by sector. A sector average is the average of the company scores in that sector, not a claim that a 70 in one sector is the same operating result as a 70 in another.
method.page.independence.title: 6. Independence
method.page.independence.text: Payment never influences a score or when it changes. Covered companies cannot buy, edit or delay their score. A company that subscribes to {product} for IR or compliance work gets the same read access as any other customer.
method.page.limitations.title: 8. Limitations
method.page.limitations.i1: Most scored companies have a short history, so the confidence tier is often provisional.
method.page.limitations.i2: The set is current listings. A company that has left the index is not carried.
method.page.limitations.i3: The decay constants, the beat floor of 60, and the minimum range width (±2% of the midpoint, and at least ±0.1 percentage point for percentage metrics) are design choices. They are not fitted to a sector's historical volatility.
method.page.limitations.i4: A statement with no number is not scored. A target for a period that has not closed stays pending, including a single-point target several years out. That target is not given a wider band.
method.page.limitations.i5: A row whose quote the fetch cannot find on the filing is left out of the score.
method.page.errors.title: 7. Reporting an error
method.page.errors.before: If you think a row is wrong, email
method.page.errors.after: with the company, period and the source you are relying on. We re-check the original filing; if the row is wrong we correct it, and the score updates when the dataset is rebuilt.

ninja.calcEmpty: No company has a closed, cited guidance row yet.
ninja.calcPath: Company level on each results date
ninja.calcMarks: The bar is the range of the four layers. The dark mark is the published year-score. A red mark above the bar is a score the formula cannot reach. The smaller mark is delivery.
ninja.calcScale: Percentage guidance uses the {rule} scale: floor {floor}, decay {decay}.
ninja.calcNoScale: This sector has no scale in the specification. Each band is measured in its own half-width.
ninja.calcBlank: This company has no closed, cited guidance row, so the delivery worksheet is blank.
ninja.heatLede: Each cell runs from 0 to 100. A darker cell is higher. A red figure is a published year-score the weights cannot reach.
ninja.testsLede: Counts of closed, cited guidance rows. No prices. Not a forecast.
